messages.author: 2c7106159c8e6d5b
messages.subject: Kinship matrix values
parts:
So, the kinship matrix values aren't quite what I expected. With pedigree data you'd expect mostly 1s along the diagonal (identity of individual and self). 

We have a DO sample. When we computed kinship with DOQTL, diagonals were all 1. When we compute kinship with qtl2, range(diag) ~ 0.52 - 0.61. I looked over some of the sample data you've made available on the rqtl2 training pages, and the self-relationship values (diagonals) can vary from sample to sample. For the French et al benzene data, diagonal values range from 0.54 to 0.71. For the grav dataset, 0.96 - 0.998. For the iron data, 0.51 - 0.82. Some of these are LOCO kinships, and some are overall, incidentally.

I'd like to understand a little better what is happening in the kinship calculations here. Thanks you for any help!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Kinship matrix values
parts:
The kinship coefficient for two individuals is: select an allele at random from each of the individual, what’s the probability the two alleles are identical by descent? For a non-inbred individual, this is 1/2. With a bit of inbreeding, it’ll be a bit > 1/2. 

See https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_relationship#Kinship_coefficient

grav dataset is for RIL. totally inbred so kinship coefficient with self is 1.

iron data is F2. 1/2 chance homozygous, 1/2 chance het. ibd probability for random alleles is 1 if homozygous and 1/2 if het, so self-self kinship coefficient for individuals will be 1/2 x 1 + 1/2 x 1/2 = 3/4. actual amount of homozygosity will vary, and so realized self-self kinship coefficient will also vary: more homozygous == large value on the diagonal.

karl
